location: Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz, south-eastern Poland

confirmed_facts.text: Objects struck three locations in south-eastern Poland on 20 November: Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz.
Polish prosecutors said on 23 November that all three objects were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles; no injuries or infrastructure damage were reported.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the incident a grave violation of Poland's airspace.

reported_claims.text: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident was likely a provocation timed to European military exercises in Poland.

international_perspectives.text: Ukraine's foreign minister said the incident shows the threat Russian aggression poses to Europe as a whole.

unknowns: Whether the missiles were deliberately aimed at Poland or strayed
Whether a Russian explanation will be offered

update_history.summary: Draft prepared for editorial review (sources accessed 23 November 2026).

title: Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles land in Poland during attacks on Ukraine
summary: Early on 20 November 2026, during large-scale Russian strikes on Ukraine, three objects came down in south-eastern Poland, a NATO member. Polish prosecutors have since said all three were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. No one was hurt. Poland's prime minister called it a likely provocation timed to European military exercises nearby, and NATO's Secretary-General called it a grave violation of Polish airspace.
impact_assessment: Observed: missile impacts on NATO territory without casualties. Potential: further airspace violations, pressure for stronger air defence along NATO's eastern flank, and escalation risk if an impact causes casualties.
priority_rationale: HIGH: confirmed weapons impacts on NATO territory with clear escalation potential, but no casualties or damage.
monitoring_actions: Follow Polish prosecutors' and Defence Ministry statements
Watch NATO statements on eastern-flank air defence
